title: Add OAuth login to the web app
bodyHtml:
Replace the homegrown password flow with OAuth (Google + GitHub) behind the oauth_login flag feature-flagged. Legacy password login stays for one release while accounts migrate.

14
files touched
3
migrations, all additive
~2 wk
to full rollout
0
expected downtime

Approach

  1. SchemaAdd an identities table and a nullable identity_id on sessions. The sessions table otherwise stays as-is.
  2. Auth endpointsNew GET /auth/:provider and callback routes in src/auth/oauth.ts; the state parameter is a signed nonce in a short-lived cookie to block CSRF.
  3. Login UIProvider buttons replace the password form; legacy form stays behind a “use legacy login” toggle.
  4. Staged rolloutCanary to 5% of traffic for 48 hours, then full rollout.

Database changes

MigrationPurposeReversible
0041_identitiesnew identities tableyes
0042_sessions_identitynullable identity_id on sessionsyes
0043_backfilllink existing users by verified emailno — snapshot first

Session storage

Two viable approaches; this plan proposes Option A.

Pros

  • Instant revocation
  • Reuses existing sessions table

Cons

  • DB read per request

Pros

  • Stateless, no DB read

Cons

  • Revocation needs a denylist
  • Key rotation ceremony

Key changes

New and modified files:

  • src/auth/
    • oauth.ts
    • providers/google.ts
    • providers/github.ts
    • session.ts
  • src/ui/login/
    • LoginForm.tsx
    • ProviderButtons.tsx

Config change to enable the flow:

@@ config/auth.ts @@
-  strategy: 'password',
+  strategy: 'oauth',
+  providers: ['google', 'github'],
   sessionTtl: '30d',
Risk: the callback endpoint is unauthenticated by design — rate-limit it at the edge.

Rollout & testing

Integration tests hit a mock provider. Canary gates on auth success rate ≥ 99.5%.

Test matrix detail
  • New signup via Google / GitHub
  • Existing account linking by verified email
  • Provider outage → graceful fallback to legacy login
Zero-downtime: every migration is additive.
